earlier_scan.source_named: ISO code retired 2015, merged into Dzongkha [dzo]; Glottolog entry is bookkeeping-only with no descriptive works

sources.citation: Karma Tshering & George van Driem. 2019. The Grammar of Dzongkha, revised and expanded. Himalayan Linguistics Archive 7 (doi 10.5070/H918144245).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Used only for identity: ch.1 p.1 lists 'Wangdi Phodra among the eight native-Dzongkha districts, and sect. 5.8 (pp.473-474) lists 'Ada (a-thang) among the geos of 'Wangdi Phodra district, i.e. the 'Ada village' of the Ethnologue Adap entry lies inside the native Dzongkha area. A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole text for stress/accent finds no word-stress statement (only the 'stress particle' ra and the circumflex 'accent' length diacritic).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2014. Change Request Number 2014-049: adopted merge [adp] Adap into [dzo] Dzongkha (effective 2015-01-12). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p.2 sect.4(b): 'Ethnologue lists Adap [adp] as a separate language but the area in which it is spoken falls under Dzongkha [dzo] in van Driem (1998) and the lexico-statistical similarity is consistent with Adap being simply a dialect of Dzongkha [dzo].' Only source cited: van Driem 1998 Dzongkha.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th edition. Dallas: SIL International. Web entry 'Adap [adp]' (Internet Archive copy 2012).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives only: 'Region: South central, Wangdue Phodrang District, from Damphu to Shemgang, Ada village. Lexical similarity: 77% with Dzongkha [dzo], 62%-65% with Bumthangkha [kjz], 41% with Tshangla [tsj].. Comments: May be the same as Dzongkha.'
Nothing; page states the entry is retired for bookkeeping, merged into [dzo] Dzongkha via CR 2014-049; no descriptive references listed (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only work the ISO change request cites for subsuming the Adap/Ada area under Dzongkha; its ethnolinguistic introduction and phonology chapter would be the place to confirm whether the 'Wangdi Phodra / Ada speech is treated as ordinary Dzongkha and whether anything is said about stress (the 2019 revised grammar held by the project says nothing about word stress). Low priority because Dzongkha is already catalogued from Watters 2018.
